CONCERNING

ADMINISTRATION OF PROTECTION FOR WOMEN AND CHILDREN VICTIMS OF VIOLENCE

I. GENERAL

Various acts of violence against both women and children within the household and outside the household continue to increase from time to time. This condition, if without serious handling, will destroy the life of households, society, nation and state. Therefore, the Sikka Regency government is obligated to provide protection to women and children victims of violence which is an implementation of various laws and regulations, including Law Number 39 of 1999 concerning Human Rights, Law Number 23 of 2004 concerning the Elimination of Domestic Violence, Law Number 21 of 2007 concerning the Eradication of Human Trafficking, Law Number 23 of 2002 concerning Child Protection.

Protection of women and children from violence is the obligation of the Regional Government as regulated in Article 22 letter a, Law Number 32 of 2004 concerning Regional Government which states that; "that in carrying out autonomy, regions have the obligation to protect the community, maintain unity, integrity and national harmony as well as the integrity of the Unitary State of the Republic of Indonesia".

On that basis, the Sikka Regency government has taken steps as an effort to provide protection to women and children victims of violence, but has not been able to provide maximum and adequate protection against violence occurring in the social life of the community, particularly for women and children, among others caused by the still low understanding of the community regarding the rights of women and children, handling has not been well coordinated, implementation has not been sustainable, and so on. Therefore, a regulation in the form of a Regional Regulation concerning the Administration of Protection for Women and Children Victims of Violence is needed to answer as well as provide legal certainty in the protection of women and children victims from violence that occurs.

The existence of a Regional Regulation concerning the Administration of Protection for Women and Children Victims of Violence provides responsibility to the Regional Government from preventing violence to handling victims of violence. In its implementation, the Regional Government cooperates with government agencies, other regional governments and the community. In addition, adequate funding support from the government, Regional Government as well as community participation from the business sector and the community, it is hoped that violence against women and children can be reduced and even in time will be eradicated from the face of this beloved Sikka land.

Article 1

In this Regional Regulation, the following terms are defined as:

1. Region is Sikka Regency.
2. Regional Government is the Government of Sikka Regency. 3. Regent is the Regent of Sikka.
4. Regional House of Representatives, hereinafter abbreviated as DPRD, is the Regional House of Representatives of Sikka Regency. 5. Regional Secretary is the Regional Secretary of Sikka Regency.
6. Regional Apparatus Work Unit, hereinafter abbreviated as SKPD, is the Regional Apparatus Work Unit of the Regional Government of Sikka Regency.
7. Child is a person who has not reached 18 years of age, including those in the womb.
8. Victim is a woman or child who experiences acts of violence and/or threats of violence encompassing physical, sexual, psychological, economic and/or social violence, in the family, community and/or society, in conflict situations, post-conflict, and the state.
9. Implementation is all actions that include Protection, Services, and Recovery for victims of violence.
10. Protection is all efforts aimed at providing a sense of security to victims carried out by the regional government, family members, advocates/paralegals, social institutions, the community, police, prosecutors, courts or other parties.
11. Special protection is protection given to children in emergency situations, children in conflict with the law, children in minority and isolated groups, children who are economically and/or sexually exploited, children who are trafficked, children who are victims of narcotics, alcohol, psychotropic substances and other addictive substances (drugs) abuse, children who are victims of kidnapping, sale, trafficking, children who are victims of physical and/or mental violence, children who are victims of conflict experiencing physical violence or trauma, children with disabilities, and children who are victims of maltreatment and neglect.
12. Recovery is all efforts to strengthen victims of violence to be more empowered, both physically, psychologically, socially, economically, culturally and politically.
13. Implementer is a government institution as well as social institutions, religious institutions, customary institutions, in accordance with their respective duties and functions, including providing the necessary facilities for victim recovery.
14. Violence is any act and/or threat of an act that results in or may result in suffering physically, psychologically, sexually or through neglect.
15. Violence against women is any action based on gender differences that results in or may result in suffering of women physically, sexually or psychologically, including threats of certain actions, coercion or arbitrary deprivation of liberty, whether occurring in the public sphere or in private life.
16. Violence against children is any act against a child that results in suffering physically, mentally, sexually, psychologically, including neglect and abuse that threatens bodily integrity and degrades the dignity of the child.
17. Physical violence is any act that causes pain, injury, wounds or bodily defects to a person, miscarriage, unconsciousness and/or causes death.
18. Psychological violence is an act that causes fear, loss of self-confidence, loss of ability to act, feelings of helplessness and/or severe psychological suffering to a person.
19. Sexual violence is any act in the form of sexual harassment, forced sexual intercourse, forced unnatural or unwanted sexual intercourse, forced sexual intercourse with others for commercial purposes and/or certain purposes.
20. Domestic neglect is the act of neglecting women and/or children within the household scope who according to the applicable law for the person concerned or because of an agreement or contract he is obliged to provide life, care, or maintenance to that person. Neglect also applies to anyone who causes economic dependence by limiting and/or prohibiting decent work inside or outside the home so that the victim is under the control of that person.
21. Service is an action that must be immediately taken for victims when seeing, hearing and knowing that violence against victims will, is, or has occurred.
22. Assistance is all actions carried out in the form of complaint services, health, advocacy and legal aid, social rehabilitation including spiritual guidance, counseling, psychological therapy and economic empowerment, repatriation and social reintegration for the strengthening and advocacy as well as recovery of victims of violence.

26. Safe house is a temporary residence used to provide protection to victims in accordance with determined operational standards.
27. Family is the smallest unit in society consisting of husband and wife, or husband and wife and their children, or father and his children, or mother and her children, or blood relatives in direct line upward or downward up to the third degree.
28. Parents are biological father and/or mother, or stepfather and/or stepmother, or adoptive father and/or adoptive mother.
29. Society is individuals, families, groups, and social organizations and/or community organizations.

Therefore, the Sikka Regency government is obligated to provide protection to women and children victims of violence which is an implementation of various laws and regulations, including Law Number 39 of 1999 concerning Human Rights, Law Number 23 of 2004 concerning the Elimination of Domestic Violence, Law Number 21 of 2007 concerning the Eradication of Human Trafficking, Law Number 23 of 2002 concerning Child Protection.

Protection of women and children from violence is the obligation of the Regional Government as regulated in Article 22 letter a, Law Number 32 of 2004 concerning Regional Government which states that; "that in carrying out autonomy, regions have the obligation to protect the community, maintain unity, integrity and national harmony as well as the integrity of the Unitary State of the Republic of Indonesia".

On that basis, the Sikka Regency government has taken steps as an effort to provide protection to women and children victims of violence, but has not been able to provide maximum and adequate protection against violence occurring in the social life of the community, particularly for women and children, among others caused by the still low understanding of the community regarding the rights of women and children, handling has not been well coordinated, implementation has not been sustainable, and so on. Therefore, a regulation in the form of a Regional Regulation concerning the Administration of Protection for Women and Children Victims of Violence is needed to answer as well as provide legal certainty in the protection of women and children victims from violence that occurs.

The existence of a Regional Regulation concerning the Administration of Protection for Women and Children Victims of Violence provides responsibility to the Regional Government from preventing violence to handling victims of violence. In its implementation, the Regional Government cooperates with government agencies, other regional governments and the community. In addition, adequate funding support from the government, Regional Government as well as community participation from the business sector and the community, it is hoped that violence against women and children can be reduced and even in time will be eradicated from the face of this beloved Sikka land.

NUMBER 12 OF 2012

CONCERNING

ADMINISTRATION OF PROTECTION FOR WOMEN AND CHILDREN VICTIMS OF VIOLENCE

I. GENERAL

Various acts of violence against both women and children within the household and outside the household continue to increase from time to time. This condition, if without serious handling, will destroy the life of households, society, nation and state. Therefore, the Sikka Regency government is obligated to provide protection to women and children victims of violence which is an implementation of various laws and regulations, including Law Number 39 of 1999 concerning Human Rights, Law Number 23 of 2004 concerning the Elimination of Domestic Violence, Law Number 21 of 2007 concerning the Eradication of Human Trafficking, Law Number 23 of 2002 concerning Child Protection.

Protection of women and children from violence is the obligation of the Regional Government as regulated in Article 22 letter a, Law Number 32 of 2004 concerning Regional Government which states that; "that in carrying out autonomy, regions have the obligation to protect the community, maintain unity, integrity and national harmony as well as the integrity of the Unitary State of the Republic of Indonesia".

On that basis, the Sikka Regency government has taken steps as an effort to provide protection to women and children victims of violence, but has not been able to provide maximum and adequate protection against violence occurring in the social life of the community, particularly for women and children, among others caused by the still low understanding of the community regarding the rights of women and children, handling has not been well coordinated, implementation has not been sustainable, and so on. Therefore, a regulation in the form of a Regional Regulation concerning the Administration of Protection for Women and Children Victims of Violence is needed to answer as well as provide legal certainty in the protection of women and children victims from violence that occurs.

The existence of a Regional Regulation concerning the Administration of Protection for Women and Children Victims of Violence provides responsibility to the Regional Government from preventing violence to handling victims of violence. In its implementation, the Regional Government cooperates with government agencies, other regional governments and the community. In addition, adequate funding support from the government, Regional Government as well as community participation from the business sector and the community, it is hoped that violence against women and children can be reduced and even in time will be eradicated from the face of this beloved Sikka land.

Article 1

In this Regional Regulation, the following terms are defined as:

1. Region is Sikka Regency.
2. Regional Government is the Government of Sikka Regency. 3. Regent is the Regent of Sikka.

6. Regional Apparatus Work Unit, hereinafter abbreviated as SKPD, is the Regional Apparatus Work Unit of the Regional Government of Sikka Regency.
7. Child is a person who has not reached 18 years of age, including those in the womb.
8. Victim is a woman or child who experiences acts of violence and/or threats of violence encompassing physical, sexual, psychological, economic and/or social violence, in the family, community and/or society, in conflict situations, post-conflict, and the state.
9. Implementation is all actions that include Protection, Services, and Recovery for victims of violence.
10. Protection is all efforts aimed at providing a sense of security to victims carried out by the regional government, family members, advocates/paralegals, social institutions, the community, police, prosecutors, courts or other parties.
11. Special protection is protection given to children in emergency situations, children in conflict with the law, children in minority and isolated groups, children who are economically and/or sexually exploited, children who are trafficked, children who are victims of narcotics, alcohol, psychotropic substances and other addictive substances (drugs) abuse, children who are victims of kidnapping, sale, trafficking, children who are victims of physical and/or mental violence, children who are victims of conflict experiencing physical violence or trauma, children with disabilities, and children who are victims of maltreatment and neglect.
12. Recovery is all efforts to strengthen victims of violence to be more empowered, both physically, psychologically, socially, economically, culturally and politically.
13. Implementer is a government institution as well as social institutions, religious institutions, customary institutions, in accordance with their respective duties and functions, including providing the necessary facilities for victim recovery.
14. Violence is any act and/or threat of an act that results in or may result in suffering physically, psychologically, sexually or through neglect.
15. Violence against women is any action based on gender differences that results in or may result in suffering of women physically, sexually or psychologically, including threats of certain actions, coercion or arbitrary deprivation of liberty, whether occurring in the public sphere or in private life.
16. Violence against children is any act against a child that results in suffering physically, mentally, sexually, psychologically, including neglect and abuse that threatens bodily integrity and degrades the dignity of the child.
17. Physical violence is any act that causes pain, injury, wounds or bodily defects to a person, miscarriage, unconsciousness and/or causes death.
18. Psychological violence is an act that causes fear, loss of self-confidence, loss of ability to act, feelings of helplessness and/or severe psychological suffering to a person.
19. Sexual violence is any act in the form of sexual harassment, forced sexual intercourse, forced unnatural or unwanted sexual intercourse, forced sexual intercourse with others for commercial purposes and/or certain purposes.
20. Domestic neglect is the act of neglecting women and/or children within the household scope who according to the applicable law for the person concerned or because of an agreement or contract he is obliged to provide life, care, or maintenance to that person. Neglect also applies to anyone who causes economic dependence by limiting and/or prohibiting decent work inside or outside the home so that the victim is under the control of that person.
21. Service is an action that must be immediately taken for victims when seeing, hearing and knowing that violence against victims will, is, or has occurred.
22. Assistance is all actions carried out in the form of complaint services, health, advocacy and legal aid, social rehabilitation including spiritual guidance, counseling, psychological therapy and economic empowerment, repatriation and social reintegration for the strengthening and advocacy as well as recovery of victims of violence.
23. Assistant is a person or representative of an institution who has the expertise to assist victims in conducting counseling, therapy and advocacy for the strengthening and recovery of victims of violence.
24. Integrated Service Center, hereinafter abbreviated as PPT, is an institution that provides services for victims of violence, hospital-based, managed jointly in the form of medical services (including medico-legal), psychological, and legal services involving health workers, educators, social institutions, law enforcement officials, psychologists, psychiatrists, volunteer assistants and/or spiritual counselors.
25. Integrated Service Center for Women and Children Empowerment, hereinafter abbreviated as P2TP2A, is an institution for victim recovery from health, education and economic independence aspects.
26. Safe house is a temporary residence used to provide protection to victims in accordance with determined operational standards.
27. Family is the smallest unit in society consisting of husband and wife, or husband and wife and their children, or father and his children, or mother and her children, or blood relatives in direct line upward or downward up to the third degree.
28. Parents are biological father and/or mother, or stepfather and/or stepmother, or adoptive father and/or adoptive mother.
29. Society is individuals, families, groups, and social organizations and/or community organizations.

CONCERNING

ADMINISTRATION OF PROTECTION FOR WOMEN AND CHILDREN VICTIMS OF VIOLENCE

I. GENERAL

Various acts of violence against both women and children within the household and outside the household continue to increase from time to time. This condition, if without serious handling, will destroy the life of households, society, nation and state. Therefore, the Sikka Regency government is obligated to provide protection to women and children victims of violence which is an implementation of various laws and regulations, including Law Number 39 of 1999 concerning Human Rights, Law Number 23 of 2004 concerning the Elimination of Domestic Violence, Law Number 21 of 2007 concerning the Eradication of Human Trafficking, Law Number 23 of 2002 concerning Child Protection.

Protection of women and children from violence is the obligation of the Regional Government as regulated in Article 22 letter a, Law Number 32 of 2004 concerning Regional Government which states that; "that in carrying out autonomy, regions have the obligation to protect the community, maintain unity, integrity and national harmony as well as the integrity of the Unitary State of the Republic of Indonesia".

On that basis, the Sikka Regency government has taken steps as an effort to provide protection to women and children victims of violence, but has not been able to provide maximum and adequate protection against violence occurring in the social life of the community, particularly for women and children, among others caused by the still low understanding of the community regarding the rights of women and children, handling has not been well coordinated, implementation has not been sustainable, and so on. Therefore, a regulation in the form of a Regional Regulation concerning the Administration of Protection for Women and Children Victims of Violence is needed to answer as well as provide legal certainty in the protection of women and children victims from violence that occurs.

The existence of a Regional Regulation concerning the Administration of Protection for Women and Children Victims of Violence provides responsibility to the Regional Government from preventing violence to handling victims of violence. In its implementation, the Regional Government cooperates with government agencies, other regional governments and the community. In addition, adequate funding support from the government, Regional Government as well as community participation from the business sector and the community, it is hoped that violence against women and children can be reduced and even in time will be eradicated from the face of this beloved Sikka land.

CONCERNING

ADMINISTRATION OF PROTECTION FOR WOMEN AND CHILDREN VICTIMS OF VIOLENCE

I. GENERAL

Various acts of violence against both women and children within the household and outside the household continue to increase from time to time. This condition, if without serious handling, will destroy the life of households, society, nation and state. Therefore, the Sikka Regency government is obligated to provide protection to women and children victims of violence which is an implementation of various laws and regulations, including Law Number 39 of 1999 concerning Human Rights, Law Number 23 of 2004 concerning the Elimination of Domestic Violence, Law Number 21 of 2007 concerning the Eradication of Human Trafficking, Law Number 23 of 2002 concerning Child Protection.

Protection of women and children from violence is the obligation of the Regional Government as regulated in Article 22 letter a, Law Number 32 of 2004 concerning Regional Government which states that; "that in carrying out autonomy, regions have the obligation to protect the community, maintain unity, integrity and national harmony as well as the integrity of the Unitary State of the Republic of Indonesia".

On that basis, the Sikka Regency government has taken steps as an effort to provide protection to women and children victims of violence, but has not been able to provide maximum and adequate protection against violence occurring in the social life of the community, particularly for women and children, among others caused by the still low understanding of the community regarding the rights of women and children, handling has not been well coordinated, implementation has not been sustainable, and so on. Therefore, a regulation in the form of a Regional Regulation concerning the Administration of Protection for Women and Children Victims of Violence is needed to answer as well as provide legal certainty in the protection of women and children victims from violence that occurs.

The existence of a Regional Regulation concerning the Administration of Protection for Women and Children Victims of Violence provides responsibility to the Regional Government from preventing violence to handling victims of violence. In its implementation, the Regional Government cooperates with government agencies, other regional governments and the community. In addition, adequate funding support from the government, Regional Government as well as community participation from the business sector and the community, it is hoped that violence against women and children can be reduced and even in time will be eradicated from the face of this beloved Sikka land.

28. Parents are biological father and/or mother, or stepfather and/or stepmother, or adoptive father and/or adoptive mother.

CONCERNING

ADMINISTRATION OF PROTECTION FOR WOMEN AND CHILDREN VICTIMS OF VIOLENCE

I. GENERAL

Various acts of violence against both women and children within the household and outside the household continue to increase from time to time. This condition, if without serious handling, will destroy the life of households, society, nation and state. Therefore, the Sikka Regency government is obligated to provide protection to women and children victims of violence which is an implementation of various laws and regulations, including Law Number 39 of 1999 concerning Human Rights, Law Number 23 of 2004 concerning the Elimination of Domestic Violence, Law Number 21 of 2007 concerning the Eradication of Human Trafficking, Law Number 23 of 2002 concerning Child Protection.

Protection of women and children from violence is the obligation of the Regional Government as regulated in Article 22 letter a, Law Number 32 of 2004 concerning Regional Government which states that; "that in carrying out autonomy, regions have the obligation to protect the community, maintain unity, integrity and national harmony as well as the integrity of the Unitary State of the Republic of Indonesia".

On that basis, the Sikka Regency government has taken steps as an effort to provide protection to women and children victims of violence, but has not been able to provide maximum and adequate protection against violence occurring in the social life of the community, particularly for women and children, among others caused by the still low understanding of the community regarding the rights of women and children, handling has not been well coordinated, implementation has not been sustainable, and so on. Therefore, a regulation in the form of a Regional Regulation concerning the Administration of Protection for Women and Children Victims of Violence is needed to answer as well as provide legal certainty in the protection of women and children victims from violence that occurs.

The existence of a Regional Regulation concerning the Administration of Protection for Women and Children Victims of Violence provides responsibility to the Regional Government from preventing violence to handling victims of violence. In its implementation, the Regional Government cooperates with government agencies, other regional governments and the community. In addition, adequate funding support from the government, Regional Government as well as community participation from the business sector and the community, it is hoped that violence against women and children can be reduced and even in time will be eradicated from the face of this beloved Sikka land.

In this Regional Regulation, the following terms are defined as:

8. Victim is a woman or child who experiences acts of violence and/or threats of violence encompassing physical, sexual, psychological, economic and/or social violence, in the family, community and/or society, in conflict situations, post-conflict, and the state.
9. Implementation is all actions that include Protection, Services, and Recovery for victims of violence.
10. Protection is all efforts aimed at providing a sense of security to victims carried out by the regional government, family members, advocates/paralegals, social institutions, the community, police, prosecutors, courts or other parties.
11. Special protection is protection given to children in emergency situations, children in conflict with the law, children in minority and isolated groups, children who are economically and/or sexually exploited, children who are trafficked, children who are victims of narcotics, alcohol, psychotropic substances and other addictive substances (drugs) abuse, children who are victims of kidnapping, sale, trafficking, children who are victims of physical and/or mental violence, children who are victims of conflict experiencing physical violence or trauma, children with disabilities, and children who are victims of maltreatment and neglect.
12. Recovery is all efforts to strengthen victims of violence to be more empowered, both physically, psychologically, socially, economically, culturally and politically.
13. Implementer is a government institution as well as social institutions, religious institutions, customary institutions, in accordance with their respective duties and functions, including providing the necessary facilities for victim recovery.

15. Violence against women is any action based on gender differences that results in or may result in suffering of women physically, sexually or psychologically, including threats of certain actions, coercion or arbitrary deprivation of liberty, whether occurring in the public sphere or in private life.
16. Violence against children is any act against a child that results in suffering physically, mentally, sexually, psychologically, including neglect and abuse that threatens bodily integrity and degrades the dignity of the child.
17. Physical violence is any act that causes pain, injury, wounds or bodily defects to a person, miscarriage, unconsciousness and/or causes death.
18. Psychological violence is an act that causes fear, loss of self-confidence, loss of ability to act, feelings of helplessness and/or severe psychological suffering to a person.
19. Sexual violence is any act in the form of sexual harassment, forced sexual intercourse, forced unnatural or unwanted sexual intercourse, forced sexual intercourse with others for commercial purposes and/or certain purposes.
20. Domestic neglect is the act of neglecting women and/or children within the household scope who according to the applicable law for the person concerned or because of an agreement or contract he is obliged to provide life, care, or maintenance to that person. Neglect also applies to anyone who causes economic dependence by limiting and/or prohibiting decent work inside or outside the home so that the victim is under the control of that person.
21. Service is an action that must be immediately taken for victims when seeing, hearing and knowing that violence against victims will, is, or has occurred.
22. Assistance is all actions carried out in the form of complaint services, health, advocacy and legal aid, social rehabilitation including spiritual guidance, counseling, psychological therapy and economic empowerment, repatriation and social reintegration for the strengthening and advocacy as well as recovery of victims of violence.

24. Integrated Service Center, hereinafter abbreviated as PPT, is an institution that provides services for victims of violence, hospital-based, managed jointly in the form of medical services (including medico-legal), psychological, and legal services involving health workers, educators, social institutions, law enforcement officials, psychologists, psychiatrists, volunteer assistants and/or spiritual counselors.

26. Safe house is a temporary residence used to provide protection to victims in accordance with determined operational standards.
27. Family is the smallest unit in society consisting of husband and wife, or husband and wife and their children, or father and his children, or mother and her children, or blood relatives in direct line upward or downward up to the third degree.
28. Parents are biological father and/or mother, or stepfather and/or stepmother, or adoptive father and/or adoptive mother.
29. Society is individuals, families, groups, and social organizations and/or community organizations.

ADMINISTRATION OF PROTECTION FOR WOMEN AND CHILDREN VICTIMS OF VIOLENCE

I. GENERAL

Various acts of violence against both women and children within the household and outside the household continue to increase from time to time. This condition, if without serious handling, will destroy the life of households, society, nation and state. Therefore, the Sikka Regency government is obligated to provide protection to women and children victims of violence which is an implementation of various laws and regulations, including Law Number 39 of 1999 concerning Human Rights, Law Number 23 of 2004 concerning the Elimination of Domestic Violence, Law Number 21 of 2007 concerning the Eradication of Human Trafficking, Law Number 23 of 2002 concerning Child Protection.

Protection of women and children from violence is the obligation of the Regional Government as regulated in Article 22 letter a, Law Number 32 of 2004 concerning Regional Government which states that; "that in carrying out autonomy, regions have the obligation to protect the community, maintain unity, integrity and national harmony as well as the integrity of the Unitary State of the Republic of Indonesia".

On that basis, the Sikka Regency government has taken steps as an effort to provide protection to women and children victims of violence, but has not been able to provide maximum and adequate protection against violence occurring in the social life of the community, particularly for women and children, among others caused by the still low understanding of the community regarding the rights of women and children, handling has not been well coordinated, implementation has not been sustainable, and so on. Therefore, a regulation in the form of a Regional Regulation concerning the Administration of Protection for Women and Children Victims of Violence is needed to answer as well as provide legal certainty in the protection of women and children victims from violence that occurs.

The existence of a Regional Regulation concerning the Administration of Protection for Women and Children Victims of Violence provides responsibility to the Regional Government from preventing violence to handling victims of violence. In its implementation, the Regional Government cooperates with government agencies, other regional governments and the community. In addition, adequate funding support from the government, Regional Government as well as community participation from the business sector and the community, it is hoped that violence against women and children can be reduced and even in time will be eradicated from the face of this beloved Sikka land.

Article 1

In this Regional Regulation, the following terms are defined as:

1. Region is Sikka Regency.
2. Regional Government is the Government of Sikka Regency. 3. Regent is the Regent of Sikka.
4. Regional House of Representatives, hereinafter abbreviated as DPRD, is the Regional House of Representatives of Sikka Regency. 5. Regional Secretary is the Regional Secretary of Sikka Regency.
6. Regional Apparatus Work Unit, hereinafter abbreviated as SKPD, is the Regional Apparatus Work Unit of the Regional Government of Sikka Regency.
7. Child is a person who has not reached 18 years of age, including those in the womb.
8. Victim is a woman or child who experiences acts of violence and/or threats of violence encompassing physical, sexual, psychological, economic and/or social violence, in the family, community and/or society, in conflict situations, post-conflict, and the state.
9. Implementation is all actions that include Protection, Services, and Recovery for victims of violence.
10. Protection is all efforts aimed at providing a sense of security to victims carried out by the regional government, family members, advocates/paralegals, social institutions, the community, police, prosecutors, courts or other parties.
11. Special protection is protection given to children in emergency situations, children in conflict with the law, children in minority and isolated groups, children who are economically and/or sexually exploited, children who are trafficked, children who are victims of narcotics, alcohol, psychotropic substances and other addictive substances (drugs) abuse, children who are victims of kidnapping, sale, trafficking, children who are victims of physical and/or mental violence, children who are victims of conflict experiencing physical violence or trauma, children with disabilities, and children who are victims of maltreatment and neglect.
12. Recovery is all efforts to strengthen victims of violence to be more empowered, both physically, psychologically, socially, economically, culturally and politically.
13. Implementer is a government institution as well as social institutions, religious institutions, customary institutions, in accordance with their respective duties and functions, including providing the necessary facilities for victim recovery.
14. Violence is any act and/or threat of an act that results in or may result in suffering physically, psychologically, sexually or through neglect.
15. Violence against women is any action based on gender differences that results in or may result in suffering of women physically, sexually or psychologically, including threats of certain actions, coercion or arbitrary deprivation of liberty, whether occurring in the public sphere or in private life.
16. Violence against children is any act against a child that results in suffering physically, mentally, sexually, psychologically, including neglect and abuse that threatens bodily integrity and degrades the dignity of the child.
17. Physical violence is any act that causes pain, injury, wounds or bodily defects to a person, miscarriage, unconsciousness and/or causes death.
18. Psychological violence is an act that causes fear, loss of self-confidence, loss of ability to act, feelings of helplessness and/or severe psychological suffering to a person.
19. Sexual violence is any act in the form of sexual harassment, forced sexual intercourse, forced unnatural or unwanted sexual intercourse, forced sexual intercourse with others for commercial purposes and/or certain purposes.
20. Domestic neglect is the act of neglecting women and/or children within the household scope who according to the applicable law for the person concerned or because of an agreement or contract he is obliged to provide life, care, or maintenance to that person. Neglect also applies to anyone who causes economic dependence by limiting and/or prohibiting decent work inside or outside the home so that the victim is under the control of that person.
21. Service is an action that must be immediately taken for victims when seeing, hearing and knowing that violence against victims will, is, or has occurred.
22. Assistance is all actions carried out in the form of complaint services, health, advocacy and legal aid, social rehabilitation including spiritual guidance, counseling, psychological therapy and economic empowerment, repatriation and social reintegration for the strengthening and advocacy as well as recovery of victims of violence.
23. Assistant is a person or representative of an institution who has the expertise to assist victims in conducting counseling, therapy and advocacy for the strengthening and recovery of victims of violence.
24. Integrated Service Center, hereinafter abbreviated as PPT, is an institution that provides services for victims of violence, hospital-based, managed jointly in the form of medical services (including medico-legal), psychological, and legal services involving health workers, educators, social institutions, law enforcement officials, psychologists, psychiatrists, volunteer assistants and/or spiritual counselors.
25. Integrated Service Center for Women and Children Empowerment, hereinafter abbreviated as P2TP2A, is an institution for victim recovery from health, education and economic independence aspects.
26. Safe house is a temporary residence used to provide protection to victims in accordance with determined operational standards.
27. Family is the smallest unit in society consisting of husband and wife, or husband and wife and their children, or father and his children, or mother and her children, or blood relatives in direct line upward or downward up to the third degree.
28. Parents are biological father and/or mother, or stepfather and/or stepmother, or adoptive father and/or adoptive mother.
29. Society is individuals, families, groups, and social organizations and/or community organizations.

Article 8

The obligations of family and/or parents as referred to in Article 5 letters c and d, who legally have full responsibility to prevent all forms of acts of violence and protect women and children as family members.

Article 22

Budget allocation for the administration of protection for women and children victims of violence is sourced from:

a. Regional Revenue and Expenditure Budget;
b. Other legitimate revenue sources in accordance with Laws and Regulations; and
c. Other revenue sources that are non-binding in nature.

Article 21

The community may conduct supervision of the administration of protection for women and children victims of violence organized by the Regional Government through a mechanism of conveying aspirations to the Regent or to the DPRD.

CONCERNING

ADMINISTRATION OF PROTECTION FOR WOMEN AND CHILDREN VICTIMS OF VIOLENCE

I. GENERAL

Various acts of violence against both women and children within the household and outside the household continue to increase from time to time. This condition, if without serious handling, will destroy the life of households, society, nation and state. Therefore, the Sikka Regency government is obligated to provide protection to women and children victims of violence which is an implementation of various laws and regulations, including Law Number 39 of 1999 concerning Human Rights, Law Number 23 of 2004 concerning the Elimination of Domestic Violence, Law Number 21 of 2007 concerning the Eradication of Human Trafficking, Law Number 23 of 2002 concerning Child Protection.

Protection of women and children from violence is the obligation of the Regional Government as regulated in Article 22 letter a, Law Number 32 of 2004 concerning Regional Government which states that; "that in carrying out autonomy, regions have the obligation to protect the community, maintain unity, integrity and national harmony as well as the integrity of the Unitary State of the Republic of Indonesia".

On that basis, the Sikka Regency government has taken steps as an effort to provide protection to women and children victims of violence, but has not been able to provide maximum and adequate protection against violence occurring in the social life of the community, particularly for women and children, among others caused by the still low understanding of the community regarding the rights of women and children, handling has not been well coordinated, implementation has not been sustainable, and so on. Therefore, a regulation in the form of a Regional Regulation concerning the Administration of Protection for Women and Children Victims of Violence is needed to answer as well as provide legal certainty in the protection of women and children victims from violence that occurs.

The existence of a Regional Regulation concerning the Administration of Protection for Women and Children Victims of Violence provides responsibility to the Regional Government from preventing violence to handling victims of violence. In its implementation, the Regional Government cooperates with government agencies, other regional governments and the community. In addition, adequate funding support from the government, Regional Government as well as community participation from the business sector and the community, it is hoped that violence against women and children can be reduced and even in time will be eradicated from the face of this beloved Sikka land.

Article 1

In this Regional Regulation, the following terms are defined as:

1. Region is Sikka Regency.
2. Regional Government is the Government of Sikka Regency. 3. Regent is the Regent of Sikka.
4. Regional House of Representatives, hereinafter abbreviated as DPRD, is the Regional House of Representatives of Sikka Regency. 5. Regional Secretary is the Regional Secretary of Sikka Regency.
6. Regional Apparatus Work Unit, hereinafter abbreviated as SKPD, is the Regional Apparatus Work Unit of the Regional Government of Sikka Regency.
7. Child is a person who has not reached 18 years of age, including those in the womb.
8. Victim is a woman or child who experiences acts of violence and/or threats of violence encompassing physical, sexual, psychological, economic and/or social violence, in the family, community and/or society, in conflict situations, post-conflict, and the state.
9. Implementation is all actions that include Protection, Services, and Recovery for victims of violence.
10. Protection is all efforts aimed at providing a sense of security to victims carried out by the regional government, family members, advocates/paralegals, social institutions, the community, police, prosecutors, courts or other parties.
11. Special protection is protection given to children in emergency situations, children in conflict with the law, children in minority and isolated groups, children who are economically and/or sexually exploited, children who are trafficked, children who are victims of narcotics, alcohol, psychotropic substances and other addictive substances (drugs) abuse, children who are victims of kidnapping, sale, trafficking, children who are victims of physical and/or mental violence, children who are victims of conflict experiencing physical violence or trauma, children with disabilities, and children who are victims of maltreatment and neglect.
12. Recovery is all efforts to strengthen victims of violence to be more empowered, both physically, psychologically, socially, economically, culturally and politically.
13. Implementer is a government institution as well as social institutions, religious institutions, customary institutions, in accordance with their respective duties and functions, including providing the necessary facilities for victim recovery.
14. Violence is any act and/or threat of an act that results in or may result in suffering physically, psychologically, sexually or through neglect.
15. Violence against women is any action based on gender differences that results in or may result in suffering of women physically, sexually or psychologically, including threats of certain actions, coercion or arbitrary deprivation of liberty, whether occurring in the public sphere or in private life.
16. Violence against children is any act against a child that results in suffering physically, mentally, sexually, psychologically, including neglect and abuse that threatens bodily integrity and degrades the dignity of the child.
17. Physical violence is any act that causes pain, injury, wounds or bodily defects to a person, miscarriage, unconsciousness and/or causes death.
18. Psychological violence is an act that causes fear, loss of self-confidence, loss of ability to act, feelings of helplessness and/or severe psychological suffering to a person.
19. Sexual violence is any act in the form of sexual harassment, forced sexual intercourse, forced unnatural or unwanted sexual intercourse, forced sexual intercourse with others for commercial purposes and/or certain purposes.
20. Domestic neglect is the act of neglecting women and/or children within the household scope who according to the applicable law for the person concerned or because of an agreement or contract he is obliged to provide life, care, or maintenance to that person. Neglect also applies to anyone who causes economic dependence by limiting and/or prohibiting decent work inside or outside the home so that the victim is under the control of that person.
21. Service is an action that must be immediately taken for victims when seeing, hearing and knowing that violence against victims will, is, or has occurred.
22. Assistance is all actions carried out in the form of complaint services, health, advocacy and legal aid, social rehabilitation including spiritual guidance, counseling, psychological therapy and economic empowerment, repatriation and social reintegration for the strengthening and advocacy as well as recovery of victims of violence.
23. Assistant is a person or representative of an institution who has the expertise to assist victims in conducting counseling, therapy and advocacy for the strengthening and recovery of victims of violence.
24. Integrated Service Center, hereinafter abbreviated as PPT, is an institution that provides services for victims of violence, hospital-based, managed jointly in the form of medical services (including medico-legal), psychological, and legal services involving health workers, educators, social institutions, law enforcement officials, psychologists, psychiatrists, volunteer assistants and/or spiritual counselors.
25. Integrated Service Center for Women and Children Empowerment, hereinafter abbreviated as P2TP2A, is an institution for victim recovery from health, education and economic independence aspects.
26. Safe house is a temporary residence used to provide protection to victims in accordance with determined operational standards.
27. Family is the smallest unit in society consisting of husband and wife, or husband and wife and their children, or father and his children, or mother and her children, or blood relatives in direct line upward or downward up to the third degree.
28. Parents are biological father and/or mother, or stepfather and/or stepmother, or adoptive father and/or adoptive mother.
29. Society is individuals, families, groups, and social organizations and/or community organizations.

11. Special protection is protection given to children in emergency situations, children in conflict with the law, children in minority and isolated groups, children who are economically and/or sexually exploited, children who are trafficked, children who are victims of narcotics, alcohol, psychotropic substances and other addictive substances (drugs) abuse, children who are victims of kidnapping, sale, trafficking, children who are victims of physical and/or mental violence, children who are victims of conflict experiencing physical violence or trauma, children with disabilities, and children who are victims of maltreatment and neglect.
12. Recovery is all efforts to strengthen victims of violence to be more empowered, both physically, psychologically, socially, economically, culturally and politically.
13. Implementer is a government institution as well as social institutions, religious institutions, customary institutions, in accordance with their respective duties and functions, including providing the necessary facilities for victim recovery.
14. Violence is any act and/or threat of an act that results in or may result in suffering physically, psychologically, sexually or through neglect.
15. Violence against women is any action based on gender differences that results in or may result in suffering of women physically, sexually or psychologically, including threats of certain actions, coercion or arbitrary deprivation of liberty, whether occurring in the public sphere or in private life.
16. Violence against children is any act against a child that results in suffering physically, mentally, sexually, psychologically, including neglect and abuse that threatens bodily integrity and degrades the dignity of the child.
17. Physical violence is any act that causes pain, injury, wounds or bodily defects to a person, miscarriage, unconsciousness and/or causes death.
18. Psychological violence is an act that causes fear, loss of self-confidence, loss of ability to act, feelings of helplessness and/or severe psychological suffering to a person.
19. Sexual violence is any act in the form of sexual harassment, forced sexual intercourse, forced unnatural or unwanted sexual intercourse, forced sexual intercourse with others for commercial purposes and/or certain purposes.
20. Domestic neglect is the act of neglecting women and/or children within the household scope who according to the applicable law for the person concerned or because of an agreement or contract he is obliged to provide life, care, or maintenance to that person. NUMBER 12 OF 2012

CONCERNING

ADMINISTRATION OF PROTECTION FOR WOMEN AND CHILDREN VICTIMS OF VIOLENCE

I. GENERAL

Various acts of violence against both women and children within the household and outside the household continue to increase from time to time. This condition, if without serious handling, will destroy the life of households, society, nation and state. Therefore, the Sikka Regency government is obligated to provide protection to women and children victims of violence which is an implementation of various laws and regulations, including Law Number 39 of 1999 concerning Human Rights, Law Number 23 of 2004 concerning the Elimination of Domestic Violence, Law Number 21 of 2007 concerning the Eradication of Human Trafficking, Law Number 23 of 2002 concerning Child Protection.

Protection of women and children from violence is the obligation of the Regional Government as regulated in Article 22 letter a, Law Number 32 of 2004 concerning Regional Government which states that; "that in carrying out autonomy, regions have the obligation to protect the community, maintain unity, integrity and national harmony as well as the integrity of the Unitary State of the Republic of Indonesia".

On that basis, the Sikka Regency government has taken steps as an effort to provide protection to women and children victims of violence, but has not been able to provide maximum and adequate protection against violence occurring in the social life of the community, particularly for women and children, among others caused by the still low understanding of the community regarding the rights of women and children, handling has not been well coordinated, implementation has not been sustainable, and so on. Therefore, a regulation in the form of a Regional Regulation concerning the Administration of Protection for Women and Children Victims of Violence is needed to answer as well as provide legal certainty in the protection of women and children victims from violence that occurs.

The existence of a Regional Regulation concerning the Administration of Protection for Women and Children Victims of Violence provides responsibility to the Regional Government from preventing violence to handling victims of violence. In its implementation, the Regional Government cooperates with government agencies, other regional governments and the community. In addition, adequate funding support from the government, Regional Government as well as community participation from the business sector and the community, it is hoped that violence against women and children can be reduced and even in time will be eradicated from the face of this beloved Sikka land.

Violence against women is any action based on gender differences that results in or may result in suffering of women physically, sexually or psychologically, including threats of certain actions, coercion or arbitrary deprivation of liberty, whether occurring in the public sphere or in private life.

NUMBER 12 OF 2012

CONCERNING

ADMINISTRATION OF PROTECTION FOR WOMEN AND CHILDREN VICTIMS OF VIOLENCE

I. GENERAL

Various acts of violence against both women and children within the household and outside the household continue to increase from time to time. This condition, if without serious handling, will destroy the life of households, society, nation and state. Therefore, the Sikka Regency government is obligated to provide protection to women and children victims of violence which is an implementation of various laws and regulations, including Law Number 39 of 1999 concerning Human Rights, Law Number 23 of 2004 concerning the Elimination of Domestic Violence, Law Number 21 of 2007 concerning the Eradication of Human Trafficking, Law Number 23 of 2002 concerning Child Protection.

Protection of women and children from violence is the obligation of the Regional Government as regulated in Article 22 letter a, Law Number 32 of 2004 concerning Regional Government which states that; "that in carrying out autonomy, regions have the obligation to protect the community, maintain unity, integrity and national harmony as well as the integrity of the Unitary State of the Republic of Indonesia".

On that basis, the Sikka Regency government has taken steps as an effort to provide protection to women and children victims of violence, but has not been able to provide maximum and adequate protection against violence occurring in the social life of the community, particularly for women and children, among others caused by the still low understanding of the community regarding the rights of women and children, handling has not been well coordinated, implementation has not been sustainable, and so on. Therefore, a regulation in the form of a Regional Regulation concerning the Administration of Protection for Women and Children Victims of Violence is needed to answer as well as provide legal certainty in the protection of women and children victims from violence that occurs.

The existence of a Regional Regulation concerning the Administration of Protection for Women and Children Victims of Violence provides responsibility to the Regional Government from preventing violence to handling victims of violence. In its implementation, the Regional Government cooperates with government agencies, other regional governments and the community. In addition, adequate funding support from the government, Regional Government as well as community participation from the business sector and the community, it is hoped that violence against women and children can be reduced and even in time will be eradicated from the face of this beloved Sikka land.

II. ARTICLE BY ARTICLE

b. conducting cooperation in the implementation of protection of women and children from victims of violence;
c. providing support for facilities and infrastructure for the implementation of protection of women and children from victims of violence; d. allocating budget for the implementation of protection of women and children victims of violence in accordance with regional financial capacity; and
e. fostering and supervising the implementation of protection of women and children victims of violence.
(2) In implementing the obligations and responsibilities as referred to in paragraph (1), the Regent establishes programs and action activities for the protection of women and children in one Regional Action Plan as the basis for SKPD in implementing the protection of women and children victims of violence.
(3) The Regional Action Plan as referred to in paragraph (2), constitutes part of the Regional Medium-Term Development Plan. (4) Further provisions regarding the Regional Action Plan as referred to in paragraph (2), shall be regulated by Regent Regulation.

NUMBER 12 OF 2012

CONCERNING

ADMINISTRATION OF PROTECTION FOR WOMEN AND CHILDREN VICTIMS OF VIOLENCE

I. GENERAL

Various acts of violence against both women and children within the household and outside the household continue to increase from time to time. This condition, if without serious handling, will destroy the life of households, society, nation and state. Therefore, the Sikka Regency government is obligated to provide protection to women and children victims of violence which is an implementation of various laws and regulations, including Law Number 39 of 1999 concerning Human Rights, Law Number 23 of 2004 concerning the Elimination of Domestic Violence, Law Number 21 of 2007 concerning the Eradication of Human Trafficking, Law Number 23 of 2002 concerning Child Protection.

Protection of women and children from violence is the obligation of the Regional Government as regulated in Article 22 letter a, Law Number 32 of 2004 concerning Regional Government which states that; "that in carrying out autonomy, regions have the obligation to protect the community, maintain unity, integrity and national harmony as well as the integrity of the Unitary State of the Republic of Indonesia".

On that basis, the Sikka Regency government has taken steps as an effort to provide protection to women and children victims of violence, but has not been able to provide maximum and adequate protection against violence occurring in the social life of the community, particularly for women and children, among others caused by the still low understanding of the community regarding the rights of women and children, handling has not been well coordinated, implementation has not been sustainable, and so on. Therefore, a regulation in the form of a Regional Regulation concerning the Administration of Protection for Women and Children Victims of Violence is needed to answer as well as provide legal certainty in the protection of women and children victims from violence that occurs.

The existence of a Regional Regulation concerning the Administration of Protection for Women and Children Victims of Violence provides responsibility to the Regional Government from preventing violence to handling victims of violence. In its implementation, the Regional Government cooperates with government agencies, other regional governments and the community. In addition, adequate funding support from the government, Regional Government as well as community participation from the business sector and the community, it is hoped that violence against women and children can be reduced and even in time will be eradicated from the face of this beloved Sikka land.

Article 1

In this Regional Regulation, the following terms are defined as:

1. Region is Sikka Regency.
2. Regional Government is the Government of Sikka Regency. 3. Regent is the Regent of Sikka.

7. Child is a person who has not reached 18 years of age, including those in the womb.
8. Victim is a woman or child who experiences acts of violence and/or threats of violence encompassing physical, sexual, psychological, economic and/or social violence, in the family, community and/or society, in conflict situations, post-conflict, and the state.
9. Implementation is all actions that include Protection, Services, and Recovery for victims of violence.
10. Protection is all efforts aimed at providing a sense of security to victims carried out by the regional government, family members, advocates/paralegals, social institutions, the community, police, prosecutors, courts or other parties.
11. Special protection is protection given to children in emergency situations, children in conflict with the law, children in minority and isolated groups, children who are economically and/or sexually exploited, children who are trafficked, children who are victims of narcotics, alcohol, psychotropic substances and other addictive substances (drugs) abuse, children who are victims of kidnapping, sale, trafficking, children who are victims of physical and/or mental violence, children who are victims of conflict experiencing physical violence or trauma, children with disabilities, and children who are victims of maltreatment and neglect.
12. Recovery is all efforts to strengthen victims of violence to be more empowered, both physically, psychologically, socially, economically, culturally and politically.
13. Implementer is a government institution as well as social institutions, religious institutions, customary institutions, in accordance with their respective duties and functions, including providing the necessary facilities for victim recovery.
14. Violence is any act and/or threat of an act that results in or may result in suffering physically, psychologically, sexually or through neglect.
15. Violence against women is any action based on gender differences that results in or may result in suffering of women physically, sexually or psychologically, including threats of certain actions, coercion or arbitrary deprivation of liberty, whether occurring in the public sphere or in private life.
16. Violence against children is any act against a child that results in suffering physically, mentally, sexually, psychologically, including neglect and abuse that threatens bodily integrity and degrades the dignity of the child.
17. Physical violence is any act that causes pain, injury, wounds or bodily defects to a person, miscarriage, unconsciousness and/or causes death.
18. Psychological violence is an act that causes fear, loss of self-confidence, loss of ability to act, feelings of helplessness and/or severe psychological suffering to a person.
19. Sexual violence is any act in the form of sexual harassment, forced sexual intercourse, forced unnatural or unwanted sexual intercourse, forced sexual intercourse with others for commercial purposes and/or certain purposes.
20. Domestic neglect is the act of neglecting women and/or children within the household scope who according to the applicable law for the person concerned or because of an agreement or contract he is obliged to provide life, care, or maintenance to that person. Neglect also applies to anyone who causes economic dependence by limiting and/or prohibiting decent work inside or outside the home so that the victim is under the control of that person.

22. CONCERNING

ADMINISTRATION OF PROTECTION FOR WOMEN AND CHILDREN VICTIMS OF VIOLENCE

I. GENERAL

Various acts of violence against both women and children within the household and outside the household continue to increase from time to time. This condition, if without serious handling, will destroy the life of households, society, nation and state. Therefore, the Sikka Regency government is obligated to provide protection to women and children victims of violence which is an implementation of various laws and regulations, including Law Number 39 of 1999 concerning Human Rights, Law Number 23 of 2004 concerning the Elimination of Domestic Violence, Law Number 21 of 2007 concerning the Eradication of Human Trafficking, Law Number 23 of 2002 concerning Child Protection.

Protection of women and children from violence is the obligation of the Regional Government as regulated in Article 22 letter a, Law Number 32 of 2004 concerning Regional Government which states that; "that in carrying out autonomy, regions have the obligation to protect the community, maintain unity, integrity and national harmony as well as the integrity of the Unitary State of the Republic of Indonesia".

On that basis, the Sikka Regency government has taken steps as an effort to provide protection to women and children victims of violence, but has not been able to provide maximum and adequate protection against violence occurring in the social life of the community, particularly for women and children, among others caused by the still low understanding of the community regarding the rights of women and children, handling has not been well coordinated, implementation has not been sustainable, and so on. Therefore, a regulation in the form of a Regional Regulation concerning the Administration of Protection for Women and Children Victims of Violence is needed to answer as well as provide legal certainty in the protection of women and children victims from violence that occurs.

The existence of a Regional Regulation concerning the Administration of Protection for Women and Children Victims of Violence provides responsibility to the Regional Government from preventing violence to handling victims of violence. In its implementation, the Regional Government cooperates with government agencies, other regional governments and the community. In addition, adequate funding support from the government, Regional Government as well as community participation from the business sector and the community, it is hoped that violence against women and children can be reduced and even in time will be eradicated from the face of this beloved Sikka land.

Article 1

In this Regional Regulation, the following terms are defined as:

1. Region is Sikka Regency.
2. Regional Government is the Government of Sikka Regency. 3. Regent is the Regent of Sikka.
4. Regional House of Representatives, hereinafter abbreviated as DPRD, is the Regional House of Representatives of Sikka Regency. 5. Regional Secretary is the Regional Secretary of Sikka Regency.
6. Regional Apparatus Work Unit, hereinafter abbreviated as SKPD, is the Regional Apparatus Work Unit of the Regional Government of Sikka Regency.
7. Child is a person who has not reached 18 years of age, including those in the womb.
8. Victim is a woman or child who experiences acts of violence and/or threats of violence encompassing physical, sexual, psychological, economic and/or social violence, in the family, community and/or society, in conflict situations, post-conflict, and the state.
9. Implementation is all actions that include Protection, Services, and Recovery for victims of violence.
10. Protection is all efforts aimed at providing a sense of security to victims carried out by the regional government, family members, advocates/paralegals, social institutions, the community, police, prosecutors, courts or other parties.
11. Special protection is protection given to children in emergency situations, children in conflict with the law, children in minority and isolated groups, children who are economically and/or sexually exploited, children who are trafficked, children who are victims of narcotics, alcohol, psychotropic substances and other addictive substances (drugs) abuse, children who are victims of kidnapping, sale, trafficking, children who are victims of physical and/or mental violence, children who are victims of conflict experiencing physical violence or trauma, children with disabilities, and children who are victims of maltreatment and neglect.
12. Recovery is all efforts to strengthen victims of violence to be more empowered, both physically, psychologically, socially, economically, culturally and politically.
13. Implementer is a government institution as well as social institutions, religious institutions, customary institutions, in accordance with their respective duties and functions, including providing the necessary facilities for victim recovery.
14. Violence is any act and/or threat of an act that results in or may result in suffering physically, psychologically, sexually or through neglect.
15. Violence against women is any action based on gender differences that results in or may result in suffering of women physically, sexually or psychologically, including threats of certain actions, coercion or arbitrary deprivation of liberty, whether occurring in the public sphere or in private life.
16. Violence against children is any act against a child that results in suffering physically, mentally, sexually, psychologically, including neglect and abuse that threatens bodily integrity and degrades the dignity of the child.
17. Physical violence is any act that causes pain, injury, wounds or bodily defects to a person, miscarriage, unconsciousness and/or causes death.
18. Psychological violence is an act that causes fear, loss of self-confidence, loss of ability to act, feelings of helplessness and/or severe psychological suffering to a person.
19. Sexual violence is any act in the form of sexual harassment, forced sexual intercourse, forced unnatural or unwanted sexual intercourse, forced sexual intercourse with others for commercial purposes and/or certain purposes.
20. Domestic neglect is the act of neglecting women and/or children within the household scope who according to the applicable law for the person concerned or because of an agreement or contract he is obliged to provide life, care, or maintenance to that person. Neglect also applies to anyone who causes economic dependence by limiting and/or prohibiting decent work inside or outside the home so that the victim is under the control of that person.
21. Service is an action that must be immediately taken for victims when seeing, hearing and knowing that violence against victims will, is, or has occurred.
22. Assistance is all actions carried out in the form of complaint services, health, advocacy and legal aid, social rehabilitation including spiritual guidance, counseling, psychological therapy and economic empowerment, repatriation and social reintegration for the strengthening and advocacy as well as recovery of victims of violence.
23. Assistant is a person or representative of an institution who has the expertise to assist victims in conducting counseling, therapy and advocacy for the strengthening and recovery of victims of violence.
24. Integrated Service Center, hereinafter abbreviated as PPT, is an institution that provides services for victims of violence, hospital-based, managed jointly in the form of medical services (including medico-legal), psychological, and legal services involving health workers, educators, social institutions, law enforcement officials, psychologists, psychiatrists, volunteer assistants and/or spiritual counselors.
25. Integrated Service Center for Women and Children Empowerment, hereinafter abbreviated as P2TP2A, is an institution for victim recovery from health, education and economic independence aspects.
26. Safe house is a temporary residence used to provide protection to victims in accordance with determined operational standards.
27. Family is the smallest unit in society consisting of husband and wife, or husband and wife and their children, or father and his children, or mother and her children, or blood relatives in direct line upward or downward up to the third degree.
28. Parents are biological father and/or mother, or stepfather and/or stepmother, or adoptive father and/or adoptive mother.
29. Society is individuals, families, groups, and social organizations and/or community organizations.

NUMBER 12 OF 2012

CONCERNING

ADMINISTRATION OF PROTECTION FOR WOMEN AND CHILDREN VICTIMS OF VIOLENCE

I. GENERAL

Various acts of violence against both women and children within the household and outside the household continue to increase from time to time. This condition, if without serious handling, will destroy the life of households, society, nation and state. Therefore, the Sikka Regency government is obligated to provide protection to women and children victims of violence which is an implementation of various laws and regulations, including Law Number 39 of 1999 concerning Human Rights, Law Number 23 of 2004 concerning the Elimination of Domestic Violence, Law Number 21 of 2007 concerning the Eradication of Human Trafficking, Law Number 23 of 2002 concerning Child Protection.

Protection of women and children from violence is the obligation of the Regional Government as regulated in Article 22 letter a, Law Number 32 of 2004 concerning Regional Government which states that; "that in carrying out autonomy, regions have the obligation to protect the community, maintain unity, integrity and national harmony as well as the integrity of the Unitary State of the Republic of Indonesia".

On that basis, the Sikka Regency government has taken steps as an effort to provide protection to women and children victims of violence, but has not been able to provide maximum and adequate protection against violence occurring in the social life of the community, particularly for women and children, among others caused by the still low understanding of the community regarding the rights of women and children, handling has not been well coordinated, implementation has not been sustainable, and so on. Therefore, a regulation in the form of a Regional Regulation concerning the Administration of Protection for Women and Children Victims of Violence is needed to answer as well as provide legal certainty in the protection of women and children victims from violence that occurs.

The existence of a Regional Regulation concerning the Administration of Protection for Women and Children Victims of Violence provides responsibility to the Regional Government from preventing violence to handling victims of violence. In its implementation, the Regional Government cooperates with government agencies, other regional governments and the community. In addition, adequate funding support from the government, Regional Government as well as community participation from the business sector and the community, it is hoped that violence against women and children can be reduced and even in time will be eradicated from the face of this beloved Sikka land.

II. ARTICLE BY ARTICLE

Article 6

(1) The obligations and responsibilities of Regional Government as referred to in Article 5 letter a, include:

a. establishing and implementing policies, programs and activities for the protection of women and children victims of violence;
b. conducting cooperation in the implementation of protection of women and children from victims of violence;
c. providing support for facilities and infrastructure for the implementation of protection of women and children from victims of violence; d. allocating budget for the implementation of protection of women and children victims of violence in accordance with regional financial capacity; and
e. fostering and supervising the implementation of protection of women and children victims of violence.
(2) In implementing the obligations and responsibilities as referred to in paragraph (1), the Regent establishes programs and action activities for the protection of women and children in one Regional Action Plan as the basis for SKPD in implementing the protection of women and children victims of violence.
(3) The Regional Action Plan as referred to in paragraph (2), constitutes part of the Regional Medium-Term Development Plan. (4) Further provisions regarding the Regional Action Plan as referred to in paragraph (2), shall be regulated by Regent Regulation.

CHAPTER X

FINANCING

Article 18

(1) In order to achieve the objectives of protecting women and children victims of violence as referred to in Article 4, the Regional Government may cooperate with:

a. The Government;
b. Provincial government
c. Other Regencies/Cities; and
d. Non-governmental institutions.
(2) Cooperation as referred to in paragraph (1) includes: a. exchange of data and information;
b. rehabilitation of victims of violence;
c. repatriation and social reintegration; and
d. provision of evidence and witnesses in accordance with applicable law.
(3) Cooperation as referred to in paragraphs (1) and (2) shall be set forth in the form of a Joint Agreement.
